content:
Alex Chen: FYI I'm seeing sustained GPU allocation failures in gcp-us-central - about ~30% of the p100 pool flapping unhealthy. GLB metrics show a spike in 5xxs originating from that region. I opened an incident (INC-2026-0318-GPU-DEG-001). Investigating causes now.
Priya Shah: Do we know if this is a networking churn or the GPU host agent crashing? Any recent deploys to that pool?
Alex Chen: No recent deploys. Logs show healthcheck timeouts and OOM-kill style messages on the node side. snippet: `kubelet: eviction signal: memory.available < threshold` and repeated `gpus: driver reset` entries.
Marco Ruiz: Ok let's avoid a hard flip. Suggest we steer traffic off us-central gradually via GLB weight adjustments. We can do 20% steps every 2m with `--drain-duration`. That buys the pool time to recover and keeps tail latency bounded.
Jamie K: Agree - cost wise we prefer not to push everything to eu-west (higher egress). Na-west has spare GPU capacity but check regional quota. Also watch `p99 latency` when you shift.
SRE Bot: Incident INC-2026-0318-GPU-DEG-001 created by Alex Chen. Channels: #eng-sre #incident-ops. Severity: P2.
Priya Shah: Marco can you prepare the GLB command? I want graceful drain: `routectl set-weight --policy global-steer --region us-central=0.2 --region na-west=0.6 --region eu-west=0.2 --drain-duration 120s`
Marco Ruiz: Running a stepped plan. Step 1 -> reduce us-central by 15% now. Command applied:
```
# routectl v0.9.2
routectl apply --policy global-steer --set us-central=0.85,na-west=0.08,eu-west=0.07 --drain-duration=120s
```
Marco Ruiz: GLB accepted config v2026-03-18a, change-id rt-3412. Starting monitor window (5m).
deploy-bot: Routing config rt-3412 applied to GLB (global-steer) by Marco Ruiz.
Alex Chen: Posting current failing log snippet for context:
```
[2026-03-18T14:03:21Z] gpu-agent[pid:2345]: ERROR: driver reset detected, context lost
[2026-03-18T14:03:22Z] kubelet: eviction signal: memory.available < threshold, evicting pods
[2026-03-18T14:03:23Z] health-checker: probe failed status=504 target=/healthz
```
Priya Shah: Monitor checklist: (1) 5xx rate from us-central should drop, (2) overall 5xx global <= 0.5% of requests, (3) p99 latency in na-west < 120ms. If any threshold breaches for 2 consecutive minutes, rollback plan = revert to previous weights and alert infra-oncall.
Jamie K: Also FYI cost watch: if na-west CPU/spill increases > +30% we may want to nudge eu-west more to avoid saturating GPUs and causing queuing.
Marco Ruiz: 2m after step 1 metrics look good: us-central 5xx down 40%, na-west p95 unchanged, p99 +8ms. Proceeding step 2 (reduce another 15%).
Marco Ruiz: Step 2 applied: us-central=0.55, na-west=0.3, eu-west=0.15. Change-id rt-3413.
SRE Bot: Alert: na-west GPU usage increased by 18% in last 4m. No errors.
Alex Chen: Nice. Still seeing some host reprobes, but pool health gradually improving. I think driver restart cascade was triggered by a kernel upgrade last night on a subset; will follow up with infra-runbook.
Priya Shah: Heads-up to CSMs: sending a short customer note template now.
Marco Ruiz: Final step: set us-central to baseline 10% for path-dependent state (keep small traffic toward local caches), na-west=0.6, eu-west=0.3. Applied rt-3414.
deploy-bot: Routing config rt-3414 applied successfully.
Jamie K: Monitoring dashboards: all key SLIs within thresholds. We'll keep this routing until the kernel rollback patch lands. Good job on the gradual steer. :thumbsup:
Alex Chen: Marking the incident as 'mitigated' in INC-2026-0318, leaving as P2 with follow-up task to remediate kernel upgrade. Thanks team.
Priya Shah: Follow-up tasks: ticket to infra to rollback kernel on affected nodes (owner: Marco), schedule validation patch, and add a GLB automation to prefer slow-drain for GPU-heavy pools.
Marco Ruiz: Created infra ticket INF-2026-4572 and assigned. Will update ETA in 1h.
Jamie K: Nice runbook execution. Closing the loop but keep watch for any regressions over 24h.
Alex Chen: Copy. Ending thread.
